content.content:
===V17 status===
-- A project's lifecycle status: ACTIVE while worked on, ON_HOLD when paused, FINISHED when done.
-- Shown on the project's row and chosen when creating one. Existing projects default to ACTIVE.
ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE';
===V12 archived===
-- Archiving a project: instead of deleting it, mark it archived so it drops off the lists but is
-- retained. Existing projects default to not archived. A toggle on the projects page reveals the
-- archived ones; the client's page never shows them.
ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN archived BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;
===V3 projects===
-- Projects: the second domain table. A project has a name and belongs to a client (client_id FK).
-- GENERATED BY DEFAULT (not ALWAYS) so the /__test__ seed path can insert explicit fixture ids.
CREATE TABLE projects (
    id        BIGINT       GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name      VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    client_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(id)
);

The schema already has `status` (V17) and `archived` (V12) columns, so no migration is needed — the change is server (widen the client-projects query to include archived rows + seed the `archived` flag) plus front-end (filter to active by default with a toggle). lines: -     * A client's own project list, oldest id first — archived projects are excluded so a tucked-away
-     * project drops off the client's page (no toggle there).
+     * A client's own project list, oldest id first — every project (finished and archived included),
+     * each carrying its {@code status} and {@code archived} flag. The client's page shows only the
+     * ACTIVE, non-archived ones by default and reveals the finished and hidden ones on its toggle,
+     * so the list carries the flags and does the filtering without a second request.
@Query("SELECT new net.officefloor.hq.app.ProjectView(p.id, p.name, c.name, p.archived, p.status) "

The test passes. Here's a summary of the full-stack change I made.

## What changed

A client's page now shows **only their active projects** (ACTIVE status, not archived) by default, with a **"Show finished and hidden projects" toggle** that reveals the rest.

### Server
- **`ProjectRepository.findViewsByClientId`** — widened the client's project query to include archived rows (removed the `AND p.archived = FALSE` filter). It already carried each project's `status` and `archived` flag, so the front-end can now filter without a second request. Filtering moved from SQL to the UI, matching how the main projects list already works.
- **`TestSupportController` seed** — the projects seed now inserts the `archived` flag from the fixture (it previously only set `id, name, client_id, status`), so a seeded `archived: true` project is actually archived.

### Front-end (all additive, per the slot/URL-key conventions)
- **`features/clients/queries.ts`** — widened `ClientProject` to carry `status` and `archived`; added the shared `CLIENT_PROJECTS_SHOW_ALL_PARAM = 'clientProjectsAll'` URL key and an `isActiveProject` helper.
- **`features/clients/ClientProjectsTable.tsx`** — reads the `clientProjectsAll` URL key and filters to active projects unless the toggle is on. Reuses the existing `project-row-<id>` / `project-name` anchors.
- **`features/clients/show-all-projects.slot.tsx`** (new) — the toggle, a `ClientDetail` slot contribution owning the same URL key, with `data-testid="client-projects-show-all"`.

### No migration
The `status` (V17) and `archived` (V12) columns already existed, so no new Flyway migration was needed — the feature is served entirely by existing schema plus the query/seed/UI changes.

Test: `1 passed`.
